items.text: A factual claim has survived independent, repeatable tests and no rival explanation fits the evidence. Which conclusion is closest to your view?

options.label: It can be known as objectively correct while remaining open to revision.
It can be strongly supported, but never known as objectively correct.
That depends on the kind of factual claim and what the tests establish.
Calling it correct mainly records that it works for now.

items.notes: Separates fallible knowledge from certainty demands and merely practical success. The case does not by itself settle global attainability.

items.text: Which claim is closest to your view about human free will?

options.label: People sometimes act with genuine free will, whatever its correct explanation is.
People can have free will, but only if a further condition on control is met.
No human action involves genuine free will.
I do not have a settled view of whether genuine free will exists.

items.notes: Separates outright denial from theories that require special conditions; a compatibilist answer alone cannot do this.
